This is a beta of Nebula v2, which runs Super Mario Galaxy as native code built from SMGCommunity's Petari decompilation, on Windows, Linux, macOS and Android. You need your own copy of the game. A beta is for trying the game and telling me what breaks: expect faults, and keep a copy of your saves.

## Downloads

| System | Download |
|---|---|
| Windows 10 or 11 (x64) | [Nebula-Beta-Setup.exe](https://github.com/keepvaibin/nebula/releases/download/v2.0.0-beta.1/Nebula-Beta-Setup.exe) |
| Linux (x86-64) | [Nebula-Beta-Linux-x64.tar.gz](https://github.com/keepvaibin/nebula/releases/download/v2.0.0-beta.1/Nebula-Beta-Linux-x64.tar.gz) |
| macOS 12 or later (Intel and Apple silicon) | [Nebula-Beta-macOS.zip](https://github.com/keepvaibin/nebula/releases/download/v2.0.0-beta.1/Nebula-Beta-macOS.zip) |
| Android 12 or later (64-bit ARM) | [Nebula-Beta-Android.apk](https://github.com/keepvaibin/nebula/releases/download/v2.0.0-beta.1/Nebula-Beta-Android.apk) |

`SHA256SUMS` lists the SHA-256 of each download. The `.sig` and `.manifest` files are what Nebula's updates check before they install a new version. A beta is offered the next beta and the final 2.0.0; Nebula 1.0.2 is not offered the beta.

## Install

**Windows:** run `Nebula-Beta-Setup.exe`. Setup asks for your disc image and installs Nebula for your account.

**Linux:**

1. Unpack `Nebula-Beta-Linux-x64.tar.gz` (in a file manager: Extract Here; in a terminal: `tar -xzf Nebula-Beta-Linux-x64.tar.gz`). A folder named `Nebula-2.0.0-beta.1-linux-x64` appears. It holds `install.sh`, `README.txt` and two folders.
2. Open that folder in a terminal (in most file managers: right-click the empty space and choose Open in Terminal) and run `./install.sh`. If it says it cannot run, run `sh install.sh`.
3. When it asks, choose your Super Mario Galaxy disc image (a file chooser opens when `zenity` or `kdialog` is installed; otherwise type the path), then install for your account (recommended) or as a portable folder. Preparing the game takes a few minutes.
4. Start Nebula from your app menu (Nebula), or run `nebula-launch` in a terminal. On a Steam Deck, do this from Desktop Mode, then add `~/.local/share/Nebula/nebula-launch` to Steam as a non-Steam game.

If nothing seems to happen, look for a window with a message, or a file named `nebula-message.txt` beside `install.sh` (or in your home folder). If the game starts and then stops, the log is `~/.local/share/Nebula/logs/game.log`; attach it when you report the fault. The install needs the system listed under Requirements below. To remove Nebula, run `uninstall.sh` in `~/.local/share/Nebula`.

**macOS:** unzip the download and move `Nebula.app` to Applications. It runs on Intel Macs and on Apple silicon. Nebula is not signed by Apple: the first time, open it from **System Settings > Privacy & Security > Open Anyway**. On macOS 14 or earlier you can instead Control-click the app and choose Open. The included `How to open Nebula.txt` has the steps. If macOS still refuses Nebula, or Nebula says the system refused a part of it, run `xattr -dr com.apple.quarantine /Applications/Nebula.app` in Terminal (it removes the mark macOS puts on every download) and open it again. The first start shows a bar while the game prepares its graphics for your Mac. On an Intel Mac that draws with its built-in graphics on a Retina display, the first start sets UPSCALING to FSR 1. To choose a resolution yourself, set UPSCALING to OFF on the GRAPHICS page, and INTERNAL RESOLUTION appears.

**Android:** install `Nebula-Beta-Android.apk`, open it, and choose your disc image.

Nebula reads Super Mario Galaxy for Wii from North America (RMGE01), Europe (RMGP01) or Japan (RMGJ01), as an ISO, RVZ or extracted folder.

## What is in

- Native code on Windows (Direct3D 12, Direct3D 11 or Vulkan), Linux (Vulkan, on X11 and Wayland) and Android (Vulkan), and macOS (Metal).
- A home screen with Play, Settings, Benchmark and Quit.
- A check for a new version. On Windows, choosing Update closes the game and Nebula's Setup installs the new version for you. On Mac and Linux it tells you there is a new version, and you install it yourself, the way you installed this one. On Android the app downloads the new version and Android's installer asks you to confirm it.
- Upscaling, anti-aliasing, ambient occlusion, enhanced lighting and HDR options.
- On Linux, upscaling with FSR 1, FSR 3 (new in this build; its upscaler only, not its frame generation) and SGSR 2, and dynamic resolution. FSR 3 is offered when the graphics card and driver have what it needs; the log says if they do not.
- In-between pictures above 60 pictures a second. They are off by default: the game shows 60 pictures a second. To try them, open the settings, go to the GRAPHICS page, set INTERPOLATION to NATIVE, and choose a TARGET FRAME RATE (MATCH REFRESH or a rate).
- PlayStation, Steam, Steam Deck and other controllers, with gyro pointing on controllers that have motion sensors. Co-Star mode with a second controller.
- Cutscene skip with a confirmation, and dialogue speed up to Instant.
- Save import and export in the game, from a Wii, Dolphin or the Switch release, and Mii import.
- 35 achievements and play statistics.
- Nebula's own menus in 14 languages. The game offers the languages your disc holds: at most seven (English, German, French, Spanish, Italian, Dutch and Japanese).
- Error codes with a saved report.

## What is not in

- Mods. This beta has no mod support: no Mods page, no `.luma` files, no LumaKit.
- DLSS and XeSS on Linux. They are in the Windows version.
- The rework of the game's code that is still to come. This beta is the game as it stands, and the final 2.0.0 comes after that work.

## Speed

I make no promise about speed, stutters or smoothness in this beta. On a phone or tablet that runs at 120 Hz, the in-between pictures are uneven today; on a 60 Hz phone there is a little extra delay from touch to picture. The first minutes after the first start can stutter on Linux, on Windows with Vulkan and on Android while the game builds its graphics programs. On NVIDIA cards, Nebula does not use the driver's present-wait feature on Linux, which has frozen programs on some driver versions, so its pacing there may be less exact.

## What I have tried

- **Windows:** one computer with two graphics cards, on all three renderers.
- **Android:** one tablet.
- **Linux:** one laptop with an RTX 4070.
- **macOS:** one Intel MacBook Pro from 2017.

The Linux and Mac packages are also started on GitHub's test machines before each release.

## Report a fault

Report problems on the [issue tracker](https://github.com/keepvaibin/nebula/issues). Say which system, which graphics card or device and which driver or system version you have, what you were doing, and: on Windows, which renderer (Direct3D 12, 11 or Vulkan: the RENDERER row on the SYSTEM page of the settings); on Linux, X11 or Wayland.

Attach the log of the run:

- **Windows:** `%LOCALAPPDATA%\Nebula\logs\latest.log`. When Nebula stops, it shows an error code and saves a report in `%LOCALAPPDATA%\Nebula\crashes`: attach both files of it (the `.txt` and the `.dmp`).
- **Linux:** `~/.local/share/Nebula/logs/game.log` (`game.previous.log` is the run before). A portable folder keeps it in `data/logs` inside the folder. If the game could not start at all, also attach `~/.local/share/Nebula/last_error.txt`. A game started from the menu or `nebula-launch` writes this log; started from a terminal, it prints there.
- **macOS:** `~/Library/Application Support/Nebula/logs/game.log` (and `game.previous.log`).
- **Android:** choose **Share the game's log** in the settings and attach it.

If the game is slow, run the benchmark in **Settings** > **System** > **Benchmark** and choose **Send to developer** on its result, when the game offers it. The game asks first, and the default is No. It sends the graphics chip, the processor, the memory and system version, your graphics settings and the benchmark's measurements, sealed so only the developer can read it. It never sends your user or computer name, file paths, serial numbers, saves or Miis. **Show the full report** shows the exact text.

## Requirements

- **Windows:** Windows 10 (1803 or later) or Windows 11, 64-bit, with a GPU that supports Direct3D 11 or later.
- **Linux:** x86-64 with glibc 2.39 and libstdc++ 3.4.32 (GCC 13) or later (for example Ubuntu 24.04 or Fedora 40), and the Vulkan loader (`libvulkan1`) with a driver: NVIDIA's own, or Mesa's (`mesa-vulkan-drivers`, `vulkan-radeon`). Older systems such as Ubuntu 22.04 and Debian 12 will probably not start it.
- **macOS:** macOS 12 or later, on an Intel or Apple silicon Mac.
- **Android:** Android 12 or later, 64-bit ARM, Vulkan 1.1.
